description: AI safety-focused foundation model lab (Claude), led by Dario Amodei. Went public on Nasdaq Nov 19, 2026 (ticker ANT), pricing at $83/share for an $81.3B raise. Alphabet and NVIDIA each committed $10B and Microsoft roughly $1B as anchor investors buying shares in a concurrent private placement alongside the IPO.

Tel Aviv-based AI startup founded in 2023 by ex-Unit 8200 veterans Dean Leitersdorf and Moshe Shalev, building real-time 'world models' (Lucy video model, Oasis simulation model) for video generation and robot training. Previously backed by NVIDIA and Amazon at a ~$4B valuation; Amazon is reportedly in advanced talks to acquire it for around $7B, after Anthropic dropped earlier acquisition talks.

Umbrella description for a family of new private-markets vehicles Altimeter Capital (the growth/venture firm led by Brad Gerstner) is raising, reportedly totaling $3B+ as of Nov 2026 — including a ~$2.5B late-stage fund (filed as Altimeter Premier Growth IX, L.P.) plus a smaller early-stage fund, aimed at AI unicorns.

A $2.5B late-stage venture fund vehicle of Altimeter Capital Management, per its SEC Form D (filed Nov 2026, CIK 2151688). General partner officers listed are Brad Gerstner (Altimeter's founder/CEO), CFO John Kiernan III and VP Matthew Tolve; aimed at pre-IPO AI/tech companies.

Helion Energy, an Everett, WA fusion-power company developing a pulsed magneto-inertial fusion generator; OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is its largest investor and executive chairman. On Oct 22, 2026 it signed a letter of intent with the Commerce Department's CHIPS R&D office for up to $175M toward high-voltage power semiconductors, with Commerce taking a non-voting equity stake priced off Helion's Series G.

Boston-area MIT spinout (founded 2024 by CEO Cynthia Liao, CTO Josh Perozek and Prof. Tomás Palacios) developing vertical gallium-nitride (vGaN) power transistors for AI data-center power infrastructure. Raised an $11M seed round in Oct 2025 led by Playground Global; on Oct 22, 2026 signed a letter of intent with the Commerce Department's CHIPS R&D office for up to $73M.

New York-based permanent-capital holding company founded 2025, co-founded by Michael J. Lee and Alexander C. Rubin (team drawn from Scale, Palantir, Lone Pine, Silver Lake), that acquires established American service-sector businesses and rebuilds them around AI and engineering. Sequoia Capital is reportedly investing hundreds of millions alongside Sequence's ~$7.7B take-private of insurer Baldwin with Michael Dell's family office; terms of Sequoia's stake are not independently confirmed (The Information's report is paywalled).

Alphabet/DeepMind-spinout (CEO Demis Hassabis) using AI for drug discovery and design. Announced a $5B Series C on Nov 17, 2026, co-led by Sequoia Capital and Greenoaks with a16z and others joining, plus a significant but undisclosed contribution from Alphabet; this follows a $2.1B round just six months earlier. Valuation undisclosed.

San Carlos, CA robotics startup founded by Zhou Xian, building general-purpose robots (its 'Eno' wheeled robot, unveiled June 2026) powered by its GENE foundation model, trained partly via a sensor-equipped data-capture glove. Announced a $500M Series A on Nov 17, 2026 at a $3.5B post-money valuation, led by Khosla Ventures, Premji Invest and Eclipse, with NVIDIA, AMD Ventures, Samsung Next and others participating; follows a $105M seed round in 2025.

AI-infrastructure startup founded November 2025 by four ex-Microsoft engineers who built Kusto/Azure Data Explorer (incl. CEO Avner Aharoni, CTO Evgeney Ryzhyk), building a unified search/analytics engine (search, vector, graph, geospatial) for AI-agent query workloads. Emerged from stealth Nov 11, 2026 with a combined $70M seed + Series A led by Sequoia Capital and Quiet Capital, with Greenoaks and Swish Ventures participating. Company's own site could not be verified (returned a server error at research time).
